decisions.reasoning: This is decision 1 with no prior attempts (reprocesses_used: 0, retry_budget: 2) and no latest_verification — so the correct first move is to render with the standard strategy. All inspection findings that could block a render are passing: picture_area passes (480×404, no padding), pose_coverage passes at 1.0 (≥0.6 gate), one_subject passes at 1.0 (≥0.95 gate), subject_size passes (p50 0.338, p95 0.342 both under the 0.55 cap), and distance_steady passes at 1.05× (≤1.35). The headroom finding is a warn, not a fail — crown is visible on 67 % of frames which meets the 0.5 evidence-sufficiency threshold required by crown_visible gate, so head metrics can be evaluated. The face_exposure finding is also a warn (recorded-content limit, not a defect to fix). No gates have failed yet; we simply need to render to get a verification result. The standard Red Curtain composite (process.standard) is the prescribed first attempt; it addresses no specific failing gate because none have failed yet — it is the standard strategy for a first attempt. If the render then fails the separation gate, process.separation_targeted is available as a follow-up within the remaining budget. If it fails any gate that no allowed strategy addresses, reshoot would be the exit.

The latest verification for attempt_1 (processed with process.standard) passed every single gate: pose_coverage at 1.0 (≥ 0.6), one_subject at 1.0 (≥ 0.95), crown_visible at 0.67 (≥ 0.5), matte_extent at 1.017 (≥ 0.9), separation at 2.37 (≥ 1.5), head_spread at 0.007 (≤ 0.02), head_drift at 1.9 px (≤ 4.0 px), frame_count at 1800 = source, and audio_md5 equal to source. There are two warnings — headroom (crown cut on 33 % of frames) and face_exposure (gain held at ×0.80) — but warnings are recorded-content limits for the report, not defects to fix. All gates are green, the verification result is passed: true, and no further action is warranted.
